key_insight: Representations learned by independent foundation models for interatomic potentials converge to a shared, low-dimensional 'platonic' geometry, enabling direct cross-model comparison and manipulation without relying on ground-truth labels.
problem_solved: The field lacked a model-agnostic, interpretable basis to compare and diagnose learned interatomic potential representations, hindering transfer, benchmarking and trustworthy use across different foundation models.
method: Collect latent embeddings from multiple independent foundation models trained for interatomic potentials and align them into a common coordinate frame.
Quantify geometric congruence (similarity measures and alignment transforms) to reveal a consistent low-dimensional 'platonic' structure across models.
Demonstrate practical uses: embedding arithmetic (vector algebra in latent space) and ground-truth-free diagnostics to assess and combine models.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a model-agnostic toolkit to compare, combine and validate foundation models for materials/chemistry applications, improving interpretability, transferability and rapid diagnostics without needing expensive reference data.
visual_elements: Aligned embedding scatter plot showing multiple models collapsing to the same low-dimensional 'platonic' shape (color-coded by model).
Matrix or heatmap of pairwise similarity / congruence scores between model representations.
Illustration of embedding arithmetic: vector add/subtract operations producing chemically meaningful shifts (e.g., bond changes) in latent space.
Flow diagram showing ground-truth-free diagnostic pipeline: embed → align → compare → diagnose/combine.
paper_title: Platonic representation of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials
